svg.title: The four reader-side faults behind most key fob help-desk tickets
svg.desc: A 2x2 grid of reader-side fault classes. One, underpowered reader: modern multi-format readers draw 200-500 mA at 12-24 V DC while legacy ProxPoint drew 100-150 mA — the top cause of intermittent reads after an upgrade; fix by pulling a clean PoE or heavier low-voltage run instead of reusing the 22 AWG home-run. Two, cleartext wiring: Wiegand sends the card number in cleartext over ~150 m of copper, undermining even an AES-encrypted DESFire fob; fix with OSDP v2 Secure Channel, AES-128 between reader and panel. Three, metal mounting: a reader on a metal frame detunes, dropping read range from 5-10 cm to 1-2 cm; fix with 6 mm of plastic or air behind the head or an on-metal-rated reader such as iCLASS R10/R40. Four, cable noise and ground loops: RS-485 runs sharing conduit with AC, VFD or LED drivers pick up induced noise, showing up as failures that follow the HVAC schedule; fix by re-routing, adding ferrite beads and using one building ground. Before opening a fob-side ticket, swap the suspect fob to a known-good door.
svg.text: READER-SIDE TRIAGE
‘My fob doesn’t work’ — the four usual suspects
1 · UNDERPOWERED READER
Modern multi-format readers draw 200-500 mA at
12-24 V DC; legacy ProxPoint drew 100-150 mA.
The top cause of intermittent reads after an upgrade.
Fix: pull a clean PoE or heavier low-voltage run —
do not reuse the 22 AWG home-run.
2 · CLEARTEXT WIRING (WIEGAND)
Wiegand sends the card number in cleartext
over ~150 m of copper — sniffable at the cable run.
It undermines even an AES-encrypted DESFire fob.
Fix: OSDP v2 Secure Channel — AES-128 between
reader and panel; confirm panel firmware first.
3 · METAL MOUNTING
A reader on a metal frame or mullion detunes:
read range drops from 5-10 cm to 1-2 cm.
Aluminum window frames count too.
Fix: 6 mm of plastic or air behind the head, or an
on-metal-rated reader head (iCLASS R10/R40).
4 · CABLE NOISE & GROUND LOOPS
RS-485 runs sharing conduit with AC, VFD or LED
driver runs pick up induced noise.
The tell: failures that follow the HVAC schedule.
Fix: re-route the data run, ferrite beads at both
ends, one building ground — not star-ground.
Before opening a fob-side ticket: swap the suspect fob to a known-good door.
The fob is the only component that fits in a hand — that is the whole reason it gets the ticket.
